vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: mails-for-agent
Version: 1.7.0

The skill provides a standard interface for an AI agent to interact with an external email service via an API defined in SKILL.md. It includes capabilities for sending, receiving, searching, and extracting data from emails, as well as a specific endpoint for retrieving verification codes to automate service registrations. The behavior is well-documented and aligned with its stated purpose, with no evidence of malicious intent, obfuscation, or unauthorized data access.

llm.summary: The skill's requested environment variables and runtime instructions match its stated purpose (manage a mailbox and retrieve verification codes); nothing requested is disproportionate or unrelated to that goal.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (receive verification codes, send/receive email, monitor inbox) align with required env vars MAILS_API_URL, MAILS_AUTH_TOKEN, MAILS_MAILBOX and the API endpoints documented in SKILL.md. primaryEnv is set to the auth token, which is expected for a remote mailbox service.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs only HTTP calls to the declared MAILS_API_URL using the provided token and mailbox; it does not instruct reading arbitrary files or other env vars. Minor inconsistency: examples use GET /api/code?timeout=60 but Constraints state the code wait timeout max is 55 seconds — this is an internal doc mismatch that should be clarified. The skill does describe destructive/side-effecting actions (DELETE email, POST /api/send) which are expected for mailbox control but have real-world impact.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no code files — instruction-only skill. This is the lowest-risk install model because nothing will be downloaded or written by an installer.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only three env vars are required (API URL, auth token, mailbox address), which are proportionate to the stated mailbox-management functionality. There are no unrelated credentials or extra config paths requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false; the skill can be invoked autonomously (platform default). That autonomy combined with mailbox control (read/send/delete) means the skill can perform impactful actions on behalf of the agent — this is expected for an email automation skill but is a behavior the user should explicitly consent to.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears internally consistent, but before installing you should: 1) confirm the MAILS_API_URL is the official/trusted service endpoint (avoid personal servers you don't control), 2) treat MAILS_AUTH_TOKEN as a high‑privilege secret — it likely allows reading, sending, and deleting mail for the mailbox, 3) prefer creating a disposable/test mailbox for automation and testing rather than using a sensitive account, 4) verify the token's scope/permissions if possible (limit to what's needed), and 5) ask the publisher to fix the documentation mismatch about GET /api/code timeout (example uses 60s but constraints say max 55s). If you will allow autonomous agent actions, explicitly review and limit what flows the agent is permitted to execute (e.g., avoid enabling automatic DELETE operations unless intended).
